Adds elementary Sidon-set bounds and finite examples around Erdős problem 30. The original `erdos_30` statement remains `category research open`, with its existing `answer(sorry)` and proof placeholder unchanged. This contribution does not solve the conjecture or claim an improved asymptotic bound.

**Scope**

- `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/30.lean`: positive-difference counting, cardinality and range of the pointwise sumset `A + A`, the elementary sum-counting bound, a weak square-root corollary, a variance identity, six concrete natural-number Sidon witnesses, and two explicitly conditional consequences.
- `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/Basic.lean`: four supporting lemmas for ordered Sidon pairs, injectivity of positive differences, and triangular pair counts.

**Assumptions and source alignment**

- `BFRCoreBound` is an assumed rounded numerical inequality, including an assumed `N ≥ 10^12` threshold. [Balogh–Füredi–Roy, Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2103.15850) motivates the coefficient 0.998, but does not establish this threshold or rounded premise. `bfr` proves only an arithmetic consequence of the explicit assumption.
- `singer` assumes `SingerSidonExists` and returns a witness in `Finset.range (q*q+q+1)`, meaning `{0,…,q²+q}`. It does not establish a lower bound for `h`, which uses `{1,…,N}`. The general construction is not proved here.

## All 1179 Erdős conjectures are now formalized

I have utilized Claude (primarily Opus 4.6) to produce formal conjectures for **all 805 remaining Erdős problems**, completing the formalization of the entire set of 1179 conjectures, and achieving [Milestone 1: All open Erdős problems formalized](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/milestone/1) in this repo. 

I believe all conjectures adhere to the style guidelines in this repo and `lake build` does pass, making this a valid and nontrivial contribution to this project.

After [contributing the conjecture for problem 13](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/1793) I realized that formalizing the few hundred remaining conjectures basically boiled down to running a for-loop (and enough tokens to pay for it), so set out to accomplish just that.

Note that this PR contains no _proofs_, only formalizations of the conjectures.

## Question for maintainers - how to proceed?

This is a massive PR generated exclusively by frontier AI and appears to be fairly new territory for this project. That being said, I've put significant effort into making it as ready as possible by focusing on strict adherence to style guidelines, believe it's worth the time to consider, and I'd be happy to assist in whatever way makes sense to do so.

**Maintainers** - Is this PR okay as-is? Should I open up 800+ PRs? Is there a more rigorous `PR_REVIEW.md` that Claude / Gemini / GPT can use to further review the conjectures to give the maintainers confidence that this isn't a deluge of AI slop? Does it make more sense to put that sort of proof-of-work in _prior_ to merging, or do these appear correct-enough and would it make more sense to continue to apply a similar batch processing on all 1179 conjectures each time a new frontier model drops? Should I just go kick rocks and maintain my own repo?

## Methodology

There were 374 formalized `.lean` conjectures in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/` when I began, leaving 805 of the problems in the set remaining to work on.

I utilized Claude in four separate stages for each problem in the batch:

1. **Formalization** - formalize conjecture - fetch from erdosproblems.com, implement, ensure `lake build` passes (see [`FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md))
2. **Styling** - update conjecture to adhere to repo style per guidance in [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) (see [`ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md))
3. **Review** - critical review of conjecture for adherence to 60-point [CHECKLIST.md](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/CHECKLIST.md) generated from [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [`README.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/README.md). 
4. **Fixes** - apply fixes (if any) identified from review step.

The batch workflow I settled on for each stage ultimately was nothing fancy - essentially just opening up a `tmux` session on the server and leaving something like this running for days (lol):

```bash
$ cat todo-conjectures.txt | xargs -I % claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "Read FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md. Apply to problem %. Write output to conjectures/%.lean. Ensure `lake build` passes."
```

I did have to upgrade to a Claude Max subscription and hit my weekly token limit twice, so would've got this done sooner if I didn't have to wait around for that to reset. Additionally, I tried to parallelize the calls but that ended up torching through my per-session limit too fast, so I fell back on a very basic strategy of just processing the problems one at a time.

All compute was performed on a tiny e2-medium (2 vCPU, 4GB RAM) server in Google Cloud.

The repo containing the work done for this project is here: https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai

prs.body:
The `erdos_307.barrier` statement in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/307.lean` currently carries `59 ≤ #(P ∪ Q)`. That is Rosen's bound, and it follows from a mass argument alone: `P` and `Q` are disjoint and `∑ 1/p ≥ 2`.

`60` is strictly stronger and does not follow that way — the reciprocals of the first 59 primes already sum to `2.00235 > 2`, so a mass of `2` is attainable on 59 primes. Reaching 60 requires excluding the 49,961 admissible 59-element supports one at a time. That is done, `sorry`-free, as `erdos307_sixty`.

**What changes**

- left conjunct `59 ≤ #(P ∪ Q)` → `60 ≤ #(P ∪ Q)`;
- `formal_proof using lean4` repinned to the current commit and pointed at `Sixty.lean#L587` (`erdos307_sixty`), where the strengthened conjunct lives;
- docstring updated: it now cites `erdos307_sixty` (`Sixty.lean`) for the left conjunct and `erdos307_barrier_closed` (`Closed.lean`) for the right, and notes that the cardinality conjunct does not need `Q.Nonempty` — that hypothesis is retained only for the product conjunct.

**What does not change**

The product conjunct `4·10¹¹² ≤ (∏ p ∈ P, p)²` is unchanged. A stronger bound `min(∏P, ∏Q) > 3.50×10⁵⁷` is proved in the accompanying paper but is **not** formalised, so it is deliberately not asserted here.

**Axioms.** Both conjuncts depend on `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` and nothing further; neither uses `native_decide`. The prime-reciprocal evaluation is kernel-checked by `decide`.

## All 1179 Erdős conjectures are now formalized

I have utilized Claude (primarily Opus 4.6) to produce formal conjectures for **all 805 remaining Erdős problems**, completing the formalization of the entire set of 1179 conjectures, and achieving [Milestone 1: All open Erdős problems formalized](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/milestone/1) in this repo. 

I believe all conjectures adhere to the style guidelines in this repo and `lake build` does pass, making this a valid and nontrivial contribution to this project.

After [contributing the conjecture for problem 13](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/1793) I realized that formalizing the few hundred remaining conjectures basically boiled down to running a for-loop (and enough tokens to pay for it), so set out to accomplish just that.

Note that this PR contains no _proofs_, only formalizations of the conjectures.

## Question for maintainers - how to proceed?

This is a massive PR generated exclusively by frontier AI and appears to be fairly new territory for this project. That being said, I've put significant effort into making it as ready as possible by focusing on strict adherence to style guidelines, believe it's worth the time to consider, and I'd be happy to assist in whatever way makes sense to do so.

**Maintainers** - Is this PR okay as-is? Should I open up 800+ PRs? Is there a more rigorous `PR_REVIEW.md` that Claude / Gemini / GPT can use to further review the conjectures to give the maintainers confidence that this isn't a deluge of AI slop? Does it make more sense to put that sort of proof-of-work in _prior_ to merging, or do these appear correct-enough and would it make more sense to continue to apply a similar batch processing on all 1179 conjectures each time a new frontier model drops? Should I just go kick rocks and maintain my own repo?

## Methodology

There were 374 formalized `.lean` conjectures in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/` when I began, leaving 805 of the problems in the set remaining to work on.

I utilized Claude in four separate stages for each problem in the batch:

1. **Formalization** - formalize conjecture - fetch from erdosproblems.com, implement, ensure `lake build` passes (see [`FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md))
2. **Styling** - update conjecture to adhere to repo style per guidance in [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) (see [`ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md))
3. **Review** - critical review of conjecture for adherence to 60-point [CHECKLIST.md](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/CHECKLIST.md) generated from [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [`README.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/README.md). 
4. **Fixes** - apply fixes (if any) identified from review step.

The batch workflow I settled on for each stage ultimately was nothing fancy - essentially just opening up a `tmux` session on the server and leaving something like this running for days (lol):

```bash
$ cat todo-conjectures.txt | xargs -I % claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "Read FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md. Apply to problem %. Write output to conjectures/%.lean. Ensure `lake build` passes."
```

I did have to upgrade to a Claude Max subscription and hit my weekly token limit twice, so would've got this done sooner if I didn't have to wait around for that to reset. Additionally, I tried to parallelize the calls but that ended up torching through my per-session limit too fast, so I fell back on a very basic strategy of just processing the problems one at a time.

All compute was performed on a tiny e2-medium (2 vCPU, 4GB RAM) server in Google Cloud.

The repo containing the work done for this project is here: https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai

## Summary

This branch contains two related formal-record improvements:

1. `formal_proof using lean4` links for four `research solved` statements
   whose external Lean proofs exceed the repository's inline length limit;
2. a substantially sharper, source-checked API around the still-open Erdős
   #647 declarations.

## External formal-proof links

| Statement | External proof | Method |
|---|---|---|
| `erdos_291.parts.ii` | [Erdos291.lean](https://github.com/Mnehmos/llm-driven-proof-search/blob/745090ac8644c90a4b9dd40171984af6b381af4e/lean-checker/LeanChecker/Erdos/Erdos291.lean) | explicit infinite family `n = 2·3^k` via `v₃(L n) ≥ k` |
| `erdos_399.variants.cambie` | [Erdos399.lean](https://github.com/Mnehmos/llm-driven-proof-search/blob/745090ac8644c90a4b9dd40171984af6b381af4e/lean-checker/LeanChecker/Erdos/Erdos399.lean) | mod-8 fourth-power argument plus `8 ∣ n!` for `n ≥ 4` |
| `erdos_494.variants.product` | [Erdos494.lean](https://github.com/Mnehmos/llm-driven-proof-search/blob/745090ac8644c90a4b9dd40171984af6b381af4e/lean-checker/LeanChecker/Erdos/Erdos494.lean) | Steinerberger counterexample using a primitive cube root and scaling invariance |
| `erdos_1113.variants.infinitely_many_sierpinski` | [Erdos1113.lean](https://github.com/Mnehmos/llm-driven-proof-search/blob/745090ac8644c90a4b9dd40171984af6b381af4e/lean-checker/LeanChecker/Erdos/Erdos1113.lean) | Selfridge covering set transferred across an infinite odd arithmetic progression |

Each linked file compiles standalone against Mathlib with no `sorry`; headline
axioms are the standard `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

## Erdős #647 API and exact reductions

The open theorem statements are deliberately unchanged. The added API proves:

- the candidate predicate is exactly equivalent to all positive shift budgets;
- above 24, non-candidacy is exactly witnessed by one failed shift;
- explicit failed shifts exclude every `25 ≤ n ≤ 84`;
- every remaining candidate is above 84, divisible by 2520, and lies in one
  of the two formalized prime-chain families;
- short windows are exactly equivalent to fixed-depth shift budgets;
- the first open window depth is connected exactly to Sophie Germain prime
  infinitude;
- candidacy is already determined by the square-root shift prefix:

  ```lean
  Candidate n ↔
    24 < n ∧
      ∀ k, 0 < k → k < n → k < 2 * Nat.sqrt n →
        σ 0 (n - k) ≤ k + 2
  ```

The last theorem is proved from the elementary bound
`Nat.divisors.card x ≤ 2 * Nat.sqrt x`, formalized inline by an explicit
injection of divisors into two copies of `Finset.range (Nat.sqrt x)`.

## Verification and status

- Targeted compilation of `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/647.lean` passes in
  the repository's pinned toolchain.
- The only warnings in that module are its three original research-open
  `sorry` declarations.
- The new square-root-prefix theorem contains no `sorry`, `admit`, or new
  axiom.

This does **not** answer Erdős #647, prove the limit variant, or prove Sophie
Germain infinitude. It turns the original candidate condition into a smaller
exact formal obligation and records the finite/structural reductions without
claiming closure.

Happy to split the proof-link and Erdős #647 parts if maintainers prefer
separate review units.

## All 1179 Erdős conjectures are now formalized

I have utilized Claude (primarily Opus 4.6) to produce formal conjectures for **all 805 remaining Erdős problems**, completing the formalization of the entire set of 1179 conjectures, and achieving [Milestone 1: All open Erdős problems formalized](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/milestone/1) in this repo. 

I believe all conjectures adhere to the style guidelines in this repo and `lake build` does pass, making this a valid and nontrivial contribution to this project.

After [contributing the conjecture for problem 13](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/1793) I realized that formalizing the few hundred remaining conjectures basically boiled down to running a for-loop (and enough tokens to pay for it), so set out to accomplish just that.

Note that this PR contains no _proofs_, only formalizations of the conjectures.

## Question for maintainers - how to proceed?

This is a massive PR generated exclusively by frontier AI and appears to be fairly new territory for this project. That being said, I've put significant effort into making it as ready as possible by focusing on strict adherence to style guidelines, believe it's worth the time to consider, and I'd be happy to assist in whatever way makes sense to do so.

**Maintainers** - Is this PR okay as-is? Should I open up 800+ PRs? Is there a more rigorous `PR_REVIEW.md` that Claude / Gemini / GPT can use to further review the conjectures to give the maintainers confidence that this isn't a deluge of AI slop? Does it make more sense to put that sort of proof-of-work in _prior_ to merging, or do these appear correct-enough and would it make more sense to continue to apply a similar batch processing on all 1179 conjectures each time a new frontier model drops? Should I just go kick rocks and maintain my own repo?

## Methodology

There were 374 formalized `.lean` conjectures in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/` when I began, leaving 805 of the problems in the set remaining to work on.

I utilized Claude in four separate stages for each problem in the batch:

1. **Formalization** - formalize conjecture - fetch from erdosproblems.com, implement, ensure `lake build` passes (see [`FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md))
2. **Styling** - update conjecture to adhere to repo style per guidance in [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) (see [`ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md))
3. **Review** - critical review of conjecture for adherence to 60-point [CHECKLIST.md](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/CHECKLIST.md) generated from [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [`README.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/README.md). 
4. **Fixes** - apply fixes (if any) identified from review step.

The batch workflow I settled on for each stage ultimately was nothing fancy - essentially just opening up a `tmux` session on the server and leaving something like this running for days (lol):

```bash
$ cat todo-conjectures.txt | xargs -I % claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "Read FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md. Apply to problem %. Write output to conjectures/%.lean. Ensure `lake build` passes."
```

I did have to upgrade to a Claude Max subscription and hit my weekly token limit twice, so would've got this done sooner if I didn't have to wait around for that to reset. Additionally, I tried to parallelize the calls but that ended up torching through my per-session limit too fast, so I fell back on a very basic strategy of just processing the problems one at a time.

All compute was performed on a tiny e2-medium (2 vCPU, 4GB RAM) server in Google Cloud.

The repo containing the work done for this project is here: https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai

Adds a "Verified partial results" section to FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/944.lean with machine-checked cores of verified progress on the k=4, r=1 case (the six-regular subproblem isolated by Skottova-Steiner, arXiv:2508.08703, Problem 5.2). Existing statement declarations are unchanged.

Proven, no sorry / no native_decide; axioms at most [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] (singleton_edge_critical is axiom-free). The added results: singleton_edge_critical (recolouring core of the singleton lemma: a colour appearing exactly once in N(v) under a 3-colouring of G-v yields a critical edge in a 4-vertex-critical graph); comps and mem_comps (enumeration of weak compositions with a proved completeness lemma); cut_matrix_classification (exactly 21 of the 3x3 nonnegative matrices with entry sum 6 have all six permutation-diagonal sums at least 2 - the exact equality case of the Skottova-Steiner 6-edge-cut bound for (4,1)-graphs); matrix_mem_classification (bridge from the genuine matrix form to the enumerated list); turan_count_shore (floor(a^2/3) < 3a-3 for 2 <= a <= 7, excluding small 6-cut shores).

Context, verified computationally with two independent implementations and generator-completeness guards (code and certificates available on request): no 6-regular 4-vertex-critical graph exists on n <= 15 other than a unique one on n = 13 (which has critical edges), so any 6-regular (4,1)-graph has at least 16 vertices; and in any 6-regular (4,1)-graph every 6-edge-cut is either a vertex star or has both shores of size at least 15 (119,236,283,370 candidate shores excluded at size 14 alone) - hence such a graph on n <= 29 vertices is super-6-edge-connected.

Update (commit 3): adds an Erdos944.ZeroBudget sub-namespace with the zero-budget identities for the deficiency-6 shore analysis, fully proven (no sorry / no native_decide; axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]): zero_budget_edge_formula (L1: s_IJ = 6p - 6q + 2B_k - 8 for a deletion-unfrozen full vertex in a graph with max degree 6 and total deficiency 6), charge_identity (L2: 6p - s_IJ = 6q + 8 - 2B_k, the component charge identity), and double_sum_even (kappa-parity). These are the arithmetic core of the structural ("frozen kernel") programme on Problem 5.2.

Update (commit 5): adds cut_row_forcing, the row-sum equality cases of the 21-matrix classification (proven, no sorry / no native_decide; axioms [propext]): among the 21 valid 6-edge-cut matrices, row sums (3,3,0) force both nonzero rows to be (1,1,1) and row sums (6,0,0) force the nonzero row to be (2,2,2). ## All 1179 Erdős conjectures are now formalized

I have utilized Claude (primarily Opus 4.6) to produce formal conjectures for **all 805 remaining Erdős problems**, completing the formalization of the entire set of 1179 conjectures, and achieving [Milestone 1: All open Erdős problems formalized](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/milestone/1) in this repo. 

I believe all conjectures adhere to the style guidelines in this repo and `lake build` does pass, making this a valid and nontrivial contribution to this project.

After [contributing the conjecture for problem 13](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/1793) I realized that formalizing the few hundred remaining conjectures basically boiled down to running a for-loop (and enough tokens to pay for it), so set out to accomplish just that.

Note that this PR contains no _proofs_, only formalizations of the conjectures.

## Question for maintainers - how to proceed?

This is a massive PR generated exclusively by frontier AI and appears to be fairly new territory for this project. That being said, I've put significant effort into making it as ready as possible by focusing on strict adherence to style guidelines, believe it's worth the time to consider, and I'd be happy to assist in whatever way makes sense to do so.

**Maintainers** - Is this PR okay as-is? Should I open up 800+ PRs? Is there a more rigorous `PR_REVIEW.md` that Claude / Gemini / GPT can use to further review the conjectures to give the maintainers confidence that this isn't a deluge of AI slop? Does it make more sense to put that sort of proof-of-work in _prior_ to merging, or do these appear correct-enough and would it make more sense to continue to apply a similar batch processing on all 1179 conjectures each time a new frontier model drops? Should I just go kick rocks and maintain my own repo?

## Methodology

There were 374 formalized `.lean` conjectures in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/` when I began, leaving 805 of the problems in the set remaining to work on.

I utilized Claude in four separate stages for each problem in the batch:

1. **Formalization** - formalize conjecture - fetch from erdosproblems.com, implement, ensure `lake build` passes (see [`FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md))
2. **Styling** - update conjecture to adhere to repo style per guidance in [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) (see [`ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md))
3. **Review** - critical review of conjecture for adherence to 60-point [CHECKLIST.md](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/CHECKLIST.md) generated from [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [`README.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/README.md). 
4. **Fixes** - apply fixes (if any) identified from review step.

The batch workflow I settled on for each stage ultimately was nothing fancy - essentially just opening up a `tmux` session on the server and leaving something like this running for days (lol):

```bash
$ cat todo-conjectures.txt | xargs -I % claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "Read FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md. Apply to problem %. Write output to conjectures/%.lean. Ensure `lake build` passes."
```

I did have to upgrade to a Claude Max subscription and hit my weekly token limit twice, so would've got this done sooner if I didn't have to wait around for that to reset. Additionally, I tried to parallelize the calls but that ended up torching through my per-session limit too fast, so I fell back on a very basic strategy of just processing the problems one at a time.

All compute was performed on a tiny e2-medium (2 vCPU, 4GB RAM) server in Google Cloud.

The repo containing the work done for this project is here: https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai

I have utilized Claude (primarily Opus 4.6) to produce formal conjectures for **all 805 remaining Erdős problems**, completing the formalization of the entire set of 1179 conjectures, and achieving [Milestone 1: All open Erdős problems formalized](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/milestone/1) in this repo.

Note that this PR contains no _proofs_, only formalizations of the conjectures.

## Question for maintainers - how to proceed?

This is a massive PR generated exclusively by frontier AI and appears to be fairly new territory for this project. That being said, I've put significant effort into making it as ready as possible by focusing on strict adherence to style guidelines, believe it's worth the time to consider, and I'd be happy to assist in whatever way makes sense to do so.

**Maintainers** - Is this PR okay as-is? Should I open up 800+ PRs? Is there a more rigorous `PR_REVIEW.md` that Claude / Gemini / GPT can use to further review the conjectures to give the maintainers confidence that this isn't a deluge of AI slop? Does it make more sense to put that sort of proof-of-work in _prior_ to merging, or do these appear correct-enough and would it make more sense to continue to apply a similar batch processing on all 1179 conjectures each time a new frontier model drops? Should I just go kick rocks and maintain my own repo?

## Methodology

There were 374 formalized `.lean` conjectures in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/` when I began, leaving 805 of the problems in the set remaining to work on.

I utilized Claude in four separate stages for each problem in the batch:

1. **Formalization** - formalize conjecture - fetch from erdosproblems.com, implement, ensure `lake build` passes (see [`FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md))

## Summary

This branch contains two related formal-record improvements:

1. `formal_proof using lean4` links for four `research solved` statements
   whose external Lean proofs exceed the repository's inline length limit;
2. a substantially sharper, source-checked API around the still-open Erdős
   #647 declarations.

## External formal-proof links

| Statement | External proof | Method |
|---|---|---|
| `erdos_291.parts.ii` | [Erdos291.lean](https://github.com/Mnehmos/llm-driven-proof-search/blob/745090ac8644c90a4b9dd40171984af6b381af4e/lean-checker/LeanChecker/Erdos/Erdos291.lean) | explicit infinite family `n = 2·3^k` via `v₃(L n) ≥ k` |
| `erdos_399.variants.cambie` | [Erdos399.lean](https://github.com/Mnehmos/llm-driven-proof-search/blob/745090ac8644c90a4b9dd40171984af6b381af4e/lean-checker/LeanChecker/Erdos/Erdos399.lean) | mod-8 fourth-power argument plus `8 ∣ n!` for `n ≥ 4` |
| `erdos_494.variants.product` | [Erdos494.lean](https://github.com/Mnehmos/llm-driven-proof-search/blob/745090ac8644c90a4b9dd40171984af6b381af4e/lean-checker/LeanChecker/Erdos/Erdos494.lean) | Steinerberger counterexample using a primitive cube root and scaling invariance |
| `erdos_1113.variants.infinitely_many_sierpinski` | [Erdos1113.lean](https://github.com/Mnehmos/llm-driven-proof-search/blob/745090ac8644c90a4b9dd40171984af6b381af4e/lean-checker/LeanChecker/Erdos/Erdos1113.lean) | Selfridge covering set transferred across an infinite odd arithmetic progression |

Each linked file compiles standalone against Mathlib with no `sorry`; headline
axioms are the standard `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

## Erdős #647 API and exact reductions

The open theorem statements are deliberately unchanged. The added API proves:

- the candidate predicate is exactly equivalent to all positive shift budgets;
- above 24, non-candidacy is exactly witnessed by one failed shift;
- explicit failed shifts exclude every `25 ≤ n ≤ 84`;
- every remaining candidate is above 84, divisible by 2520, and lies in one
  of the two formalized prime-chain families;
- short windows are exactly equivalent to fixed-depth shift budgets;
- the first open window depth is connected exactly to Sophie Germain prime
  infinitude;
- candidacy is already determined by the square-root shift prefix:

  ```lean
  Candidate n ↔
    24 < n ∧
      ∀ k, 0 < k → k < n → k < 2 * Nat.sqrt n →
        σ 0 (n - k) ≤ k + 2
  ```

The last theorem is proved from the elementary bound
`Nat.divisors.card x ≤ 2 * Nat.sqrt x`, formalized inline by an explicit
injection of divisors into two copies of `Finset.range (Nat.sqrt x)`.

## Verification and status

- Targeted compilation of `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/647.lean` passes in
  the repository's pinned toolchain.
- The only warnings in that module are its three original research-open
  `sorry` declarations.
- The new square-root-prefix theorem contains no `sorry`, `admit`, or new
  axiom.

This does **not** answer Erdős #647, prove the limit variant, or prove Sophie
Germain infinitude. It turns the original candidate condition into a smaller
exact formal obligation and records the finite/structural reductions without
claiming closure.

Happy to split the proof-link and Erdős #647 parts if maintainers prefer
separate review units.

|---|---|---|
| `erdos_291.parts.ii` | [Erdos291.lean](https://github.com/Mnehmos/llm-driven-proof-search/blob/745090ac8644c90a4b9dd40171984af6b381af4e/lean-checker/LeanChecker/Erdos/Erdos291.lean) | explicit infinite family `n = 2·3^k` via `v₃(L n) ≥ k` |
| `erdos_399.variants.cambie` | [Erdos399.lean](https://github.com/Mnehmos/llm-driven-proof-search/blob/745090ac8644c90a4b9dd40171984af6b381af4e/lean-checker/LeanChecker/Erdos/Erdos399.lean) | mod-8 fourth-power argument plus `8 ∣ n!` for `n ≥ 4` |
| `erdos_494.variants.product` | [Erdos494.lean](https://github.com/Mnehmos/llm-driven-proof-search/blob/745090ac8644c90a4b9dd40171984af6b381af4e/lean-checker/LeanChecker/Erdos/Erdos494.lean) | Steinerberger counterexample using a primitive cube root and scaling invariance |

Each linked file compiles standalone against Mathlib with no `sorry`; headline
axioms are the standard `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

## Erdős #647 API and exact reductions

The open theorem statements are deliberately unchanged. The added API proves:

- the candidate predicate is exactly equivalent to all positive shift budgets;
- above 24, non-candidacy is exactly witnessed by one failed shift;
- explicit failed shifts exclude every `25 ≤ n ≤ 84`;
- every remaining candidate is above 84, divisible by 2520, and lies in one
  of the two formalized prime-chain families;
- short windows are exactly equivalent to fixed-depth shift budgets;
- the first open window depth is connected exactly to Sophie Germain prime
  infinitude;
- candidacy is already determined by the square-root shift prefix:

  ```lean
  Candidate n ↔
    24 < n ∧
      ∀ k, 0 < k → k < n → k < 2 * Nat.sqrt n →
        σ 0 (n - k) ≤ k + 2
  ```

The last theorem is proved from the elementary bound
`Nat.divisors.card x ≤ 2 * Nat.sqrt x`, formalized inline by an explicit
injection of divisors into two copies of `Finset.range (Nat.sqrt x)`.

## Verification and status

- Targeted compilation of `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/647.lean` passes in
  the repository's pinned toolchain.
- The only warnings in that module are its three original research-open
  `sorry` declarations.
- The new square-root-prefix theorem contains no `sorry`, `admit`, or new
  axiom.

This does **not** answer Erdős #647, prove the limit variant, or prove Sophie
Germain infinitude. It turns the original candidate condition into a smaller
exact formal obligation and records the finite/structural reductions without
claiming closure.

Happy to split the proof-link and Erdős #647 parts if maintainers prefer
separate review units.

prs.body:
## All 1179 Erdős conjectures are now formalized

I have utilized Claude (primarily Opus 4.6) to produce formal conjectures for **all 805 remaining Erdős problems**, completing the formalization of the entire set of 1179 conjectures, and achieving [Milestone 1: All open Erdős problems formalized](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/milestone/1) in this repo. 

I believe all conjectures adhere to the style guidelines in this repo and `lake build` does pass, making this a valid and nontrivial contribution to this project.

After [contributing the conjecture for problem 13](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/1793) I realized that formalizing the few hundred remaining conjectures basically boiled down to running a for-loop (and enough tokens to pay for it), so set out to accomplish just that.

Note that this PR contains no _proofs_, only formalizations of the conjectures.

## Question for maintainers - how to proceed?

This is a massive PR generated exclusively by frontier AI and appears to be fairly new territory for this project. That being said, I've put significant effort into making it as ready as possible by focusing on strict adherence to style guidelines, believe it's worth the time to consider, and I'd be happy to assist in whatever way makes sense to do so.

**Maintainers** - Is this PR okay as-is? Should I open up 800+ PRs? Is there a more rigorous `PR_REVIEW.md` that Claude / Gemini / GPT can use to further review the conjectures to give the maintainers confidence that this isn't a deluge of AI slop? Does it make more sense to put that sort of proof-of-work in _prior_ to merging, or do these appear correct-enough and would it make more sense to continue to apply a similar batch processing on all 1179 conjectures each time a new frontier model drops? Should I just go kick rocks and maintain my own repo?

## Methodology

There were 374 formalized `.lean` conjectures in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/` when I began, leaving 805 of the problems in the set remaining to work on.

I utilized Claude in four separate stages for each problem in the batch:

1. **Formalization** - formalize conjecture - fetch from erdosproblems.com, implement, ensure `lake build` passes (see [`FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md))
2. **Styling** - update conjecture to adhere to repo style per guidance in [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) (see [`ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md))
3. **Review** - critical review of conjecture for adherence to 60-point [CHECKLIST.md](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/CHECKLIST.md) generated from [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [`README.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/README.md). 
4. **Fixes** - apply fixes (if any) identified from review step.

The batch workflow I settled on for each stage ultimately was nothing fancy - essentially just opening up a `tmux` session on the server and leaving something like this running for days (lol):

```bash
$ cat todo-conjectures.txt | xargs -I % claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "Read FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md. Apply to problem %. Write output to conjectures/%.lean. Ensure `lake build` passes."
```

I did have to upgrade to a Claude Max subscription and hit my weekly token limit twice, so would've got this done sooner if I didn't have to wait around for that to reset. Additionally, I tried to parallelize the calls but that ended up torching through my per-session limit too fast, so I fell back on a very basic strategy of just processing the problems one at a time.

All compute was performed on a tiny e2-medium (2 vCPU, 4GB RAM) server in Google Cloud.

The repo containing the work done for this project is here: https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai

- State part (a) as one set-level characterization of all qualifying composite integers, instead of a separate proposition-valued answer after each `n` has been bound.

The source asks to characterize the composite integers satisfying `f(n) = n / P(n)`. ## All 1179 Erdős conjectures are now formalized

I have utilized Claude (primarily Opus 4.6) to produce formal conjectures for **all 805 remaining Erdős problems**, completing the formalization of the entire set of 1179 conjectures, and achieving [Milestone 1: All open Erdős problems formalized](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/milestone/1) in this repo. 

I believe all conjectures adhere to the style guidelines in this repo and `lake build` does pass, making this a valid and nontrivial contribution to this project.

After [contributing the conjecture for problem 13](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/1793) I realized that formalizing the few hundred remaining conjectures basically boiled down to running a for-loop (and enough tokens to pay for it), so set out to accomplish just that.

Note that this PR contains no _proofs_, only formalizations of the conjectures.

## Question for maintainers - how to proceed?

This is a massive PR generated exclusively by frontier AI and appears to be fairly new territory for this project. That being said, I've put significant effort into making it as ready as possible by focusing on strict adherence to style guidelines, believe it's worth the time to consider, and I'd be happy to assist in whatever way makes sense to do so.

**Maintainers** - Is this PR okay as-is? Should I open up 800+ PRs? Is there a more rigorous `PR_REVIEW.md` that Claude / Gemini / GPT can use to further review the conjectures to give the maintainers confidence that this isn't a deluge of AI slop? Does it make more sense to put that sort of proof-of-work in _prior_ to merging, or do these appear correct-enough and would it make more sense to continue to apply a similar batch processing on all 1179 conjectures each time a new frontier model drops? Should I just go kick rocks and maintain my own repo?

## Methodology

There were 374 formalized `.lean` conjectures in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/` when I began, leaving 805 of the problems in the set remaining to work on.

I utilized Claude in four separate stages for each problem in the batch:

1. **Formalization** - formalize conjecture - fetch from erdosproblems.com, implement, ensure `lake build` passes (see [`FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md))
2. **Styling** - update conjecture to adhere to repo style per guidance in [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) (see [`ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md`](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/ADHERE_TO_DEEPMIND_STYLE.md))
3. **Review** - critical review of conjecture for adherence to 60-point [CHECKLIST.md](https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai/blob/master/CHECKLIST.md) generated from [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [`README.md`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/README.md). 
4. **Fixes** - apply fixes (if any) identified from review step.

The batch workflow I settled on for each stage ultimately was nothing fancy - essentially just opening up a `tmux` session on the server and leaving something like this running for days (lol):

```bash
$ cat todo-conjectures.txt | xargs -I % claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "Read FORMALIZE_CONJECTURE.md. Apply to problem %. Write output to conjectures/%.lean. Ensure `lake build` passes."
```

I did have to upgrade to a Claude Max subscription and hit my weekly token limit twice, so would've got this done sooner if I didn't have to wait around for that to reset. Additionally, I tried to parallelize the calls but that ended up torching through my per-session limit too fast, so I fell back on a very basic strategy of just processing the problems one at a time.

All compute was performed on a tiny e2-medium (2 vCPU, 4GB RAM) server in Google Cloud.

The repo containing the work done for this project is here: https://github.com/ryantuck/erdos-ai
